title: New York Sirens returning to Madison Square Garden after last season’s record-setting debut
content:
Playing at Madison Square Garden was once something the New York Sirens could hardly imagine.

“Ever since day one in New York, it was kind of a pipe dream,” Sirens captain Micah Zandee-Hart told The Athletic. “It was like, ‘Oh, imagine if we could play at Madison Square Garden,’ and we would kind of joke about it.”

Last April, that dream became reality.

More than 18,000 fans packed the Garden for the arena’s first Professional Women’s Hockey League game, watching the Sirens defeat the Seattle Torrent 2-1 in a shootout. The sellout crowd set a U.S. attendance record for professional women’s hockey and marked a return of major professional women’s team sports to MSG, where the WNBA’s New York Liberty last played in 2017.

“Thinking back to that moment, I honestly have chills,” Zandee-Hart said.

Now, the league is returning for round two.

This year, the New York Sirens will take on the Detroit Clutch at Madison Square Garden on Jan. 23, 2027.

“What we experienced at Madison Square Garden last April was truly special, a memorable moment for our organization, our league and women’s hockey,” said Sirens general manager Pascal Daoust. “Having the privilege of returning to The World’s Most Famous Arena gives us another opportunity to showcase the excellence of our game.”

The PWHL’s return to the Garden will also serve as a reunion of sorts. New York’s Sarah Fillier and Maja Nylén Persson, who helped secure April’s shootout victory, will face a Detroit expansion team featuring Hilary Knight and Cayla Barnes, both of whom represented Seattle in that game. Former Sirens forward Taylor Girard will also be back at MSG, this time playing for the Clutch.

The decision to feature one of the league’s four new expansion teams at Madison Square Garden is notable as the PWHL looks to build on its rapid growth. Since launching with six teams in January 2024, the league has doubled in size to 12 franchises in less than three years, while average regular-season attendance has climbed 71 percent. The matchup will give Detroit an early national showcase at one of hockey’s most recognizable venues as the PWHL introduces its newest teams to a growing audience.

For Zandee-Hart, the league’s return to the Garden is another sign of how far women’s hockey has come.

“It shows our growth, and it shows that it’s something people want to see and will come to. The more opportunities we have to play those big games, fill those seats and set those historic benchmarks, we’ve definitely proven that we’re ready to do that.”

The Garden, for its part, is eager to welcome the league back after last season’s record-setting debut.

“The response from PWHL fans was tremendous, and we can’t wait to build on it with another memorable night of hockey on the biggest stage in sports,” said Joel Fisher, executive vice president of MSG Marquee Events and Operations.
